newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Moody's rates CITIC HK foreign currency debt Baa3.
newsitem.headline: Moody's rates CITIC HK foreign currency debt Baa3.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Thursday it assigned Baa3 to the long-term foreign currency debt of about US$225 million guaranteed by China International Trust & Investment Corp Hong Kong (Holdings) Ltd (CITIC HK).
The rating includes the 20 billion yen seven-year bonds issued in December 1996 by its subsidiary CITIC Hong Kong Finance (Cayman) Ltd, the rating agency said in a statement.
The rating reflects the critical position of CITIC HK in the group structure of the Beijing-based China International Trust and Investment Corp (CITIC), Moody's said.
CITIC HK, the holding company for CITIC's Hong Kong interests, controls conglomerate CITIC Pacific Ltd.
The CITIC group's principal profit earner has been its investment in CITIC Pacific, while CITIC's other major subsidiary is CITIC Industrial Bank, China's sixth largest commercial bank.
Moody's said CITIC HK does not represent a stronger credit than CITIC, nor of its main China-based subsidiary CITIC Industrial Bank.

The agency rates CITIC Industrial Bank Baa3 for its long-term foreign currency deposits and debt. It rates CITIC Baa1 for its long-term foreign currency debt as these obligations are expected to receive more support from the Chinese government.

Moody's said it rates the long-term debt guaranteed by CITIC Pacific Baa2 and the outlook for this rating is positive, given the company's increasing experience and the development and growing maturity of China's economy.
